### U459 — **W-43: producer authenticity for approval decisions, and what it does NOT prove**

**CLOSED at `aea1e8a`.** [[U206]] — a `decision` event over an approvable row was honored whatever
wrote it, and `tests/unit/test_session_approvals.py:297` memorialized that as expected behaviour.
That test is INVERTED and RENAMED; it failed against pre-repair code on its assertion
(`assert feed["sourced"] is False` / `assert True is False`), not on a missing symbol.

**The mechanism.** `route_session_decision` stamps the decision record with an HMAC over its own
canonical bytes; `_apply_decision` — the one boundary that decides whether a recorded decision
affects approval state — verifies it before the authority is consulted. Not distributed across
approval types. Signed: the whole `decision` object minus the stamp, so a field added later is signed
by default and an added field breaks the stamp. Not signed: `event_id`, `at`, `provenance` — the
reducer reads none of them and the shell re-stamps the first two on append, so signing them would
break every genuine decision while protecting nothing. Domain-separated from W-41's envelope HMAC by
a `SOW_APPROVAL_DECISION_V1\x00` prefix, so an authenticated envelope cannot be transplanted;
W-41's `canonical_payload` is the DONOR, because two serializers that can disagree is a bypass.

**The key** is minted once per shell process in `approvals/drawer-source.js` — the one module that
spawns BOTH emitters — and handed to each in its environment. Not `process.env` (one forgotten scrub
from leaking into a pane), not a file beside the log (readable by whoever can write the log, so it
would authenticate the forger too). Its lifetime is the log's, because `begin()` truncates once per
process, which is why no session identifier had to be invented to stop a cross-session replay.

**Three existing tests would have been SHADOWED** by the new outer guard. Their events are
authentically stamped and each now asserts WHICH guard refused — `invariant 1`, `invariant 16`,
`no approval item`. Holding the session key does not widen authority, and the assertions are what
prove the inner guards are still reached. The standing rule earned its keep for the fourth time.

**STILL OPEN, unchanged:** [[U205]] — a well-made forged UTTERANCE or plan row. W-43 authenticates
the DECISION producer only and does not claim otherwise. And [[U207]] — who is at the keyboard is
still presumed. The module's HONEST RESIDUAL says both, and says that U206 is closed exactly as far
as the key's confidentiality reaches: an attacker who can read the shell's process memory is inside
the supervisor's containment boundary already, which is a different problem than a file anyone can
append to.

### U460 — **U458 CORRECTIVE: signature parity restored across the two implementations**

**CLOSED at `eef7262`.** [[U458]]'s repair, and the standing rule it produced.

**Python was NOT weakened back.** The Node mirror was brought forward:
`apps/desktop/ipc/envelope.js` now signs and verifies the WHOLE envelope minus `integrity`, reusing
its existing serializer rather than growing a second one, and `makeEnvelope` assembles the object
THEN signs it — the tag used to be computed inside the object literal, over a value that did not yet
contain the fields the signature is supposed to cover, which is what made the defect easy to write
and invisible to review. Python's `make_envelope` was restructured the same way at W-41 for the same
reason; that the two files diverged in structure as well as in behaviour is part of how this went
unnoticed.

**THE GOLDEN VECTOR CAME FIRST, and it is the durable part of this unit.** Nothing in the tree
compared the two implementations, so nothing could have caught W-41's regression. One fixed envelope
— nested objects, non-ASCII, an astral character, an array, a boolean, a null, top-level keys
deliberately unsorted — is now canonicalized and HMAC'd by both sides under one fixed secret and
compared byte-for-byte (`tests/unit/test_envelope_cross_language_parity.py`, via a probe that calls
the PRODUCTION module and reimplements nothing). Verified failing pre-repair: **12 failed, 1 passed**,
the decisive one a value mismatch with both byte forms printed.

**What that failure showed, and it is not what one would guess.** The SERIALIZERS never disagreed:
`canonicalPayload` and `canonical_payload` produce identical bytes for the hostile vector, key
sorting and UTF-8 included. What was wrong was the INPUT handed to them. So a byte-equality test
alone does not grade the regression — the HMAC comparison does — and the mutation row is graded
accordingly.

**Freshness parity, previously owed.** The Node side gained `envelopeIsFresh` and
`FRESHNESS_WINDOW_S`, pinned equal to Python's MECHANICALLY by a test that reads both constants
rather than trusting a comment. It is enforced in `client.js` on every reply, in the gateway's own
ruled order (integrity, then the signed `ts`) — a verification rule with no caller is not a check.
A NAIVE timestamp is refused explicitly, because `Date.parse` would silently read it as LOCAL time
and the window would then mean something different on every host.

**Tamper coverage on the NODE side, proved rather than inherited.** W-41 proved the Python receiver;
[[U458]] is the proof that this was insufficient, because the shell is a receiver too. Eight fields
rewritten independently, each refused — and every one of those tests FIRST asserts the untampered
envelope verifies. That correction came from this unit's own false pass: the cross-language tamper
test passed pre-repair precisely because a signature covering nothing satisfies every `is False`.

**THE STANDING RULE this unit adds, and it is the reason the unit exists:** *when a repair changes a
wire format, a serialization, or a shared constant, ask what the OTHER implementation does — before
the boundary asks for you.* W-41 passed all eleven of its own acceptance properties and still shipped
this, because every property tested one side of a two-sided protocol.

### U458 — **CORRECTIVE B: classified, and it was the fixtures, not the product**

Recorded as its own disposition because the classification was the work, and the wrong answer would
have produced a repair to shipped code that was never broken.

**The PRODUCT path is sound** [OBSERVED]. `main.js` assigns `gatewayProc` immediately after
`spawn()` — before the handshake can fail — and `teardown()` kills it while the quit path awaits
`waitForChildExit(gatewayProc)`. A failed bootstrap in the shipped shell does not leak a gateway.

**The TEST FIXTURES leaked.** `supervisor.test.js` killed its private gateway inline after an
assertion; `recovery-live.test.js` killed its gateway on the last line of the test body. Neither was
fenced, so the first failing assertion skipped both, the child kept its stdout piped to the runner,
and the event loop never drained. Both are `try/finally` now, and `killAndWait` WAITS for the exit
instead of merely signalling — recovery-live's version would itself have hung forever on an
already-exited child, the same class of bug one level down, reached only by the fence that now calls
it on whatever `gw` currently is.

**MEASURED, by re-injecting the exact U458 signing defect:**

| | `supervisor.test.js` |
|---|---|
| before the teardown repair | exit 124, 90s, never returned |
| after | exit 1, 1s, with a full report |

**No shorter `--test-timeout` was used.** A timeout makes the corpse easier to find; it does not bury
it, and the leaked gateway would still hold a port. The runner's `--test-timeout=0` is recorded as an
INSTRUMENT OBSERVATION — it is why forty minutes produced no output at all — and it was not allowed
to substitute for cleanup.

**New acceptance, proven from OUTSIDE the process that would leak**, because *"this process exits"*
is only observable to a parent: a real wrong-key bootstrap failure, in its own process, must exit on
its own AND leave its gateway reaped. Falsified — commenting out the reap turns it RED.

**A defect in that acceptance test, caught by the suite it was written for.** Its first version
counted `run_gateway` processes machine-wide; it passed run alone and FAILED in the full desktop
suite, which runs these files concurrently and had four sibling gateways up. It is scoped to the
fixture's own pid now — and to that pid's CHILDREN, since killing a `py.exe` launcher and orphaning
the `python.exe` it started is not reaping. The same "measured in the wrong process" shape [[U455]]
recorded.

### Tier 3 — **CLOSED / ACCEPTED by the operator, 2026-08-17**

Recorded so no later reader has to reconstruct it from the boundary tables. The acceptance was
explicit that the requirement was never *"make the desktop suite green somehow"* but: explain the
regression, prove causality, repair the correct layer, then rerun the complete boundary on a
**stationary committed tree**. The W-41 corrective was accepted on the ground that Python's
full-envelope authentication stayed intact and the Node peer was brought into parity rather than the
stronger side being weakened.

**Two calls recorded at the operator's instruction, because they generalise:**

  1. `makeEnvelope` **assembling then signing**, rather than computing the tag inside the object
     literal over a value that does not yet contain the signed fields. *That shape is what made the
     original defect easy to write and invisible to review.*
  2. Catching this unit's **own false pass** — the cross-language tamper test passed pre-repair
     because a signature covering nothing satisfies every `is False`. **Asserting that the
     untampered artifact verifies FIRST is now the standard for every tamper suite in this
     programme.**

**And the framing that must survive summarisation, because it stops a wrong future repair:** the
serializers were ALREADY byte-equivalent. `canonicalPayload` and `canonical_payload` agree on nested
objects, non-ASCII, astral characters and key order. **The defect was which object was handed to the
serializer.** Anyone who reads "cross-language canonicalization bug" and sets out to fix
canonicalization will be fixing something that was never broken. Grading mutation O20 by HMAC
comparison rather than byte equality follows directly from this and is not an implementation detail.

**Corrective B accepted as a FIXTURE lifecycle defect, not a product one**, on the evidence that the
product records the gateway before handshake failure and reaps it on the awaited quit path while the
fixtures placed cleanup after assertions with no `finally`. `killAndWait` waiting rather than
signalling — since recovery-live's version would itself have hung on an already-dead child — is
recorded as the same bug one level down.

### The TWO STANDING RULES, now part of the review discipline

Both are operator-ruled and apply to every remaining unit:

  1. **When a repair changes a wire format, serialization contract, shared constant, protocol field,
     or cross-runtime semantic — enumerate every independent implementation before claiming closure,
     and prove parity across the boundary.** W-41 is the textbook case: Python became more secure,
     Node remained historically correct by its own tests, and together they produced a dead control
     channel. *Both were locally plausible; the system was broken.*
  2. **When an outer validation rule changes, verify that tests for inner guards still reach the
     inner guard they claim to exercise.**

### U462 — **W-44: the antigravity listing read prose as models, and layout as nothing**

**CLOSED at `c7f2308`.** Tier 4's first unit. Governing root cause for the tier, unchanged:
*provider control state must not be inferred authoritatively from arbitrary provider prose when
structured process or status evidence exists.*

**Two defects in eight lines, pulling in OPPOSITE directions** — which is why neither half could be
repaired alone, and why a tab-split-only fix would have made the second strictly worse. The filter
was `if not line or line.endswith(":") or " " in line: continue`.

**Measured before any repair, end to end** [OBSERVED]:

    inventory from the word Traceback: ('Traceback',) | note: ok
    roster model_ref: {'resolved_slug': 'Traceback', 'verified': True,
      'note': "per-node model 'Traceback', confirmed present in the CLI's own listing"}
    picker would OFFER: ('Traceback',)

`Error`, `unauthenticated`, `Warning`, `FAILED`, `None`, `null`, `true` behaved identically. The
other direction returned `()` — an EMPTY inventory, failing the picker closed for a working provider
— for every bullet, tab-column and space-column listing. **And a third variant that is worse than
either:** `gemini-3-pro (default)` was dropped while its unannotated sibling survived and
`parse_note` still said `ok` — a silently PARTIAL inventory, the one outcome neither the operator nor
a later reader can detect.

**Repaired on the `parse_grok_models` three-axis precedent:** what a line may be (optional bullet,
slug, rest); what a SLUG may be (alphanumeric runs joined by single separators, carrying at least one
digit or separator — *a model id is not an English word*); and what may follow it (nothing, a
`(default)`/`(current)` annotation, or a display column introduced by a STRUCTURAL delimiter — a tab
or a run of two-or-more spaces, never a single space).

**The two axes are not redundant, and each catches what the other cannot.** Axis 3 catches
`gpt-4 is not available in your region`, whose first token is a genuine model id and which a shape
rule alone would admit. Axis 2 catches `Traceback (most recent call last)`, whose tail has the shape
of an annotation and which an annotation rule alone would admit.

**Rejected-line reporting added to `parse_note`, going one step beyond grok:** grok says nothing
about rejects when it found no models, which is exactly the prose-only page that most needs saying.
An empty inventory from a traceback and an empty inventory from an empty listing are different facts.

**DELIBERATE BOUND, recorded rather than left to be discovered:** a model id that is a single
alphabetic word with no digit — a hypothetical `sonnet` — is refused. That is the fail-closed
direction, and the line is COUNTED in `parse_note`, so the refusal is visible instead of looking like
an empty listing.

**Negative tests verified failing pre-repair: 19 failed / 200 passed**, every one on a value. The
picker-surface test was falsified separately against `HEAD`'s parser
(`assert ('Traceback',) == ()`), because the parser returning `()` and the picker offering nothing
are two facts and the unit is only worth anything if the second follows.

**TWO mutation rows, one per direction** (`_op18e_hardening_mutations.py` H11/H12), each graded by a
test the other's mutation leaves green — a single row would let half the repair be deleted silently,
which is the shape of the original defect. 12/12 RED; the sibling harness anchoring the same file
11/11 RED; python-suite 2612 passed / 2 skipped / 0 failed.

### U463 — **RECORDED: where the `probe_status` / `probe_provider_cli` duplication actually is**

Recorded while executing W-44, NOT repaired, so the next unit does not re-derive it. The tier's
instruction permits unifying cross-provider policy **only where the duplication itself caused the
defect**, and this is where that duplication lives.

Two independent probe paths select a provider's listing parser by DIFFERENT mechanisms:

  * `adapters/frontier/provider_cli_common.py:probe_provider_cli` takes `parse_models=` as a
    parameter — the adapter passes its own parser in;
  * `tools/providers/frontier_provider_recon.py:probe_status` hard-codes the choice inline:
    `parse_grok_models(out) if spec.provider == GROK_PROVIDER else parse_antigravity_models(out)`.

So a third provider added to the recon path silently gets the ANTIGRAVITY parser by falling through
the `else`. That is a latent instance of exactly the class W-44 repaired — a provider's output read
by a parser written for a different provider's format — and it is not hypothetical arithmetic: the
`else` branch is the default for every provider that is not grok.

**Not repaired here.** W-44's scope was the parser, its diff was three files, and widening it to
restructure two probe entry points would have been the abstraction rewrite the tier explicitly
forbids. **Owner: whichever Tier-4 unit covers the probe split.**

### U464 — **W-45 (A-7): an HTTP status code is not a model id**

**CLOSED at `925a7ab`.** Expected to be MEASURED / NO-REPAIR, covered by W-44. It was not, and the
measurement is the unit. Ten of the eleven A-7 rows were already refused; a bare `401` was not:

    inventory from a bare 401: ('401',) | note: ok
    picker would OFFER: ('401',)
    roster model_ref: {'resolved_slug': '401', 'verified': True,
      'note': "per-node model '401', confirmed present in the CLI's own listing"}

`403`, `429`, `500` and `4-0-1` behaved identically. **Why W-44 missed it, and the distinction is

The correction is one predicate on the same axis — an id must also carry a LETTER — and explicitly
**not** a list of auth words, which would have greened the observed rows while leaving every future
status code minted. **W-44 therefore did not fully satisfy its stated family repair.**

**CLOSED at `4f9c499`.** `_GROK_LOGIN_MARKER_RE` was applied with `.search()` over an UNANCHORED
pattern, so any line CONTAINING the phrase reported a session. Four measured, including two that say

— on the ONLY auth evidence available without a live call.

already an exact-line comparison. **Declared bound:** a line that begins declaratively and then

### U466 — **W-47 (R-05): six ways of saying "not signed in" authenticated**

**CLOSED at `179cbad`.** `CodexCli.login_status` asked `any("logged in" in low)` and then subtracted
an exact-substring blacklist. "logged in" is a substring of every signed-out sentence that NAMES the
state it is denying, so each phrasing outside the list authenticated at rc==0: *no longer logged in*,
*not currently logged in*, *were logged in previously*, *never logged in*, *aren't logged in*, and
**"Failed to check whether you are logged in"** — a message saying the CHECK ITSELF FAILED, read as
success.

rc==0 is correct in all of them (a signed-out report is a SUCCESSFUL call), so the exit code was
never going to catch this. Repaired by reading the SHAPE of the sentence: a login report is a
DECLARATION and must open the line. The blacklist is KEPT as defence in depth, and because it is no
longer the gate **its reachability is now proven separately** — otherwise the pre-existing "Not
logged in" test would have been passing on the anchor alone while claiming to exercise the list.

`adapters/frontier/codex.py` was anchored by **no mutation harness at all** before this unit
(verified by grep, not assumed). It has one now.

### U467 — **W-48 (A-6): an answer about rate limits is not a rate limit**

**CLOSED at `4d8f87c`.** `CodexCliBackend.generate` scanned the WHOLE of a zero-exit stdout for the
auth/credit/rate markers, so a successful answer whose SUBJECT was one of them raised
`CodexAuthError` — a **NODE-WIDE pause**, not a task-level failure. Five measured; asking the model
how to rate-limit an endpoint took the node down. The only escape was `out.startswith("{")`: an
answer survived by being JSON.

Repaired on the tier hierarchy — rc==0 is STRUCTURED evidence the call succeeded, and structured
evidence outranks prose. The branch is NOT deleted (an auth condition really can surface on a zero
exit) but narrowed to text that READS AS AN ERROR REPORT. **An error report DECLARES the condition;
an answer MENTIONS it.** The NON-ZERO path is deliberately unchanged and is now pinned as its own
test, so the two paths cannot be collapsed into one rule later.

**Declared bound:** a zero-exit auth report in some OTHER shape is not paused by this path. Pausing a
whole node on an answer is worse than missing a signal that the non-zero path, the `login status`
probe and the launch gate all also carry.

### U468 — **W-49 (R-08): one models-call auth policy, two callers — and [[U463]] discharged**

**CLOSED at `12fc368`.** `probe_status` and `probe_provider_cli` carried SEPARATE COPIES of the same
policy and had drifted in two ways at once. On the shape the REAL CLI uses — grok writes its
declarative auth line to STDERR, inventory on stdout, exit 0:

    probe_status        auth_state = UNVERIFIED     | models = ('grok-4.5',)
    probe_provider_cli  auth_state = AUTHENTICATED  | models = ('grok-4.5',)

  1. **STDERR.** One parsed `out + err`, the other `out` alone. *Which stream the parser sees is AUTH
     POLICY, not a formatting detail* — which is exactly why it must not live in two places.
  2. **AUTH-REQUIRED EVIDENCE.** `probe_status` had **no `auth_required_reported` branch at all**: it
     parsed the evidence and dropped it one line later, so a CLI explicitly reporting that the
     operator is signed out was recorded as merely UNVERIFIED and `state` stayed AVAILABLE.

`classify_models_call` is now the one implementation; both probes call it, and a test asserts they
reach the SAME FUNCTION OBJECT — two names for one policy is the same failure one step later.
`confirm_hint` is the single presentational knob, because a second copy carrying a different sentence
is how this drifted the first time.

**[[U463]] DISCHARGED.** The spec now NAMES its parser as a REQUIRED field, so no provider can fall
through the old `else` and be read by the antigravity parser. A required field cannot be fallen
through. **Agreement across all four shapes is asserted as its own property**, because "both were
repaired" and "both now answer the same thing" are different claims, and R-08 asks for the second.

### U469 — **RECORDED: a repair script silently converted three product files to CRLF**

Caught during W-45, recorded because it damaged EVIDENCE before it was noticed and the mechanism will
recur.

A helper script used Python `write_text`, which on Windows translates the newline to CRLF. All three
files became 100% CRLF **in the worktree**. The commit would still have been LF — `.gitattributes`
normalises, and `git diff` looked clean — but **the worktree bytes are what a mutation harness
reads**, so every MULTI-LINE anchor went `SKIPPED-ANCHOR-MISSING` while single-line anchors still
matched. **The harness reported a plausible 10/13 instead of failing.**

Caught only because H3 and H4 — rows that unit never touched — went skipped. The files were
normalised back and re-verified with `git ls-files --eol`; the harness then reported 13/13.

**The general shape, which is [[U461]] again from the other side:** an instrument that reports a
PARTIAL result is more dangerous than one that fails, because a partial result looks like an answer.
`git ls-files --eol` is the check (want `w/lf`; only `docs/loop/LOOP_STATE.json` is legitimately
`w/mixed`, being D-4 material).

### STANDING RULE — **a partial mutation count is an INSTRUMENT FAILURE, not a score**

Operator-ruled from [[U469]], and it applies to every harness in this tree from here on.

> **Harness setup must FAIL CLOSED if any declared mutation row is skipped because its anchor is
> absent or the pinned bytes no longer match.** A partial mutation count is not a valid result
> unless the harness explicitly declares which rows are legitimately non-applicable.

| observed | reading |
|---|---|
| `18/18 CAUGHT` | **evidence** |
| `0/18`, stale pin | **instrument failure** |
| `10/13` + 3 SKIPPED on byte drift | **instrument failure** |

**Never let "10 caught, 3 skipped" read as 77% assurance. This is falsification, not a high-school
exam.** A harness that reports a partial result is claiming to have measured something it did not
measure, which is strictly worse than one that refuses to start — the same shape as [[U461]], where
a harness dead at its pin check let six units believe they had falsification coverage.

**It also reinforces the re-pin rule: compare RAW WORKTREE BYTES, not `git diff`.** Git
normalisation reports a clean tree while a byte-pinned harness sees different content — which is
exactly how [[U469]] stayed invisible until two untouched rows went skipped.

**NOT YET IMPLEMENTED.** This is recorded as the governing rule; making the six harnesses fail
closed on a skipped row belongs with the hygiene unit that owns [[U461]], and must not become
another supervisory layer.

### U470 — **W-50 (R-24): `generate()` consumes the classifier verdict**

**CLOSED at `ba0f778`.** The structured verdict was in hand and thrown away: the pause was
re-derived by searching `outcome.detail`, which is `redact_diagnostics(stderr or stdout)` — ONE
stream, and at most `MAX_DIAGNOSTIC_CHARS` (600) of it — while the classifier had already read BOTH
streams in full. Measured, two independent mechanisms:

    verdict=AUTH_REQUIRED  rescan_says_pause=False  <- auth on STDOUT, ordinary stderr
    verdict=AUTH_REQUIRED  rescan_says_pause=False  <- auth beyond the 600-char redaction limit

In both a real authentication failure became an ordinary `RuntimeError` and **the node was never
paused**. The verdict is the fact; the detail is a human-readable excerpt, and **an excerpt is not
evidence**.

**The repair is narrower than a parser change** — no classifier touched, no marker list widened.
`USAGE_LIMIT` is consumed alongside `AUTH_REQUIRED` and pinned separately, since taking only the
auth verdict would leave rate/quota an ordinary failure.

**A SECOND LIVE `generate` PATH was included deliberately.** `CodexCliBackend.generate` classified
`stderr or stdout` and had the identical wrong-stream miss — an auth failure on stdout with any
stderr noise raised `RuntimeError`. Acceptance 1 is a property of the SYSTEM and this build has two
live generate paths; shipping the unit with it false on one of them would be the *looks stronger
than it is* artifact this programme refuses. The codex fix is minimal: classify over both streams,
leave its marker vocabulary and its excerpt alone.

**TEST 3 WAS REWRITTEN MID-UNIT, and the reason is recorded in the test.** A first attempt tried to
straddle an auth marker across the two streams and **cannot**: the classifier joins them with a
newline, so a contiguous marker never spans the boundary. **Stream SYMMETRY** is the property that
is actually true and actually matters — a per-stream rule answers differently depending on where the
CLI happened to print, which is the defect itself.

**TEST 6 asserts its own premise before using it**: for each construction it first checks that the
classifier says `AUTH_REQUIRED` *and* that `is_auth_pause_text(outcome.detail)` is FALSE. The
excerpt reaching `generate` therefore provably carries none of the trigger prose, so any downstream
re-scan must answer "no pause". That is what proves CONSUMPTION rather than coincidental
re-derivation — and it cannot pass by accident if `redact_diagnostics` ever changes.

**Tests 1/2/4/5 passed BEFORE the repair and are the control, not the evidence.** "stdout-only" with
an EMPTY stderr happened to work, because `stderr or stdout` then fell through to stdout. It took
stderr *noise* to expose the defect — which is why test 6 had to exist.

**H20 answered the question H19 could not.** It empties the structured auth verdict while leaving
the auth prose intact in both streams and in the excerpt. Had it stayed GREEN, the downstream path
would still be rediscovering authority from prose and the duplicated policy would still exist. **It
is RED**, so the verdict is the only thing consulted.

### U471 — **W-51 (R-25): an empty inventory is an absence of evidence, not a permission**

**CLOSED at `03db9f3`.** `resolve_model_ref` refused an out-of-inventory slug ONLY when `available`
was truthy, so an EMPTY or UNESTABLISHED inventory disabled the very check meant to stop an
unverified label. Measured before repair:

    resolve_model_ref("attacker-or-unprobed-label", ())
      -> slug='attacker-or-unprobed-label'   (carried "unverified")
    build_command
      -> ['agy', '--mode', 'plan', '--model', 'attacker-or-unprobed-label', ...]

**SURVEYED BEFORE EDITING.** `resolve_model_ref` has exactly two production callers — the
`roster_descriptor` of each OP-12 provider — so the policy was fixed THERE, in one place, and no
validation was copied into any argv builder. `None` is untouched and is NOT an unverified label: it
still means *omit the flag, let the CLI use its own configured default*, pinned as its own test
including that `build_command` emits no `--model` at all.

**THE TWO EMPTY STATES REACH THE SAME DECISION AND ARE NOT THE SAME FACT.** `available is None` says
**NOT ESTABLISHED**; `()` says **EMPTY**. Both refuse an explicit request; the diagnostics differ and
a test asserts that they differ. Collapsing them is how "empty" starts reading as "fine" — the
optimistic reading of emptiness that [[U462]]/[[U464]] repaired one layer up, which is why the
cross-unit case is pinned: a parser refusing a provider's error page leaves no trustworthy inventory,
and an arbitrary caller label still cannot escape through `--model`.

**THREE EXISTING TESTS asserted the OLD carried-unverified behaviour** and were re-examined rather
than blindly updated. Each moved from *"published but not verified"* to *"not published at all"*,
which is strictly stronger; the roster-shape test is now asked with a CORROBORATED model and its
uncorroborated form became its own refusal test.

**THE FIRST MUTATION ATTEMPT WAS WRONG, and the finding is the durable part.** Simply DELETING the
two guards left H22 **GREEN**: with the empty branch gone, `slug not in inventory` refuses `()`
anyway. **So the empty branch does not carry the REFUSAL — it carries the DIAGNOSTIC** that keeps the
two absences distinct. *Deleting a guard whose job is a diagnostic is invisible to a test that only
asserts a raise.* Both rows now RESTORE THE OLD RETURN (`carried unverified`), which is the behaviour
that actually shipped, and both go RED.

| this OpenCode leg | FAIL | **PASS in 96.83 s** |

**That is the whole distinction.** The Ollama legs fail in isolation, so they are a genuine
COLD-MODEL READINESS defect. This one passes in isolation and only fails under load, so it is
RESOURCE CONTENTION / SUITE INTERACTION. Its 240 s budget is ample on a quiet host and inadequate
while the same host is concurrently running the rest of the suite — including, plausibly, the three
Ollama legs each spending up to 180 s trying to cold-load a 17–67 GB model on the same runtime.
**That last link is a hypothesis consistent with the evidence, not a measured fact**, and it is
written as one.

**IT DOES NOT GET ITS OWN SKIP-WITH-RECORD, and that is deliberate.** A skip criterion here could
only mean *"the host is busy"* — the one general "external stuff seems unhappy" switch that must not
be built. There is nothing about the PREREQUISITE that is unsatisfied: opencode is present, the coder
model is present, and the drive completes correctly when given the machine. The honest dispositions
are serialization of the live legs, or removing the contention at its source — which the [[U472]]
readiness guard would do as a side effect, since a leg that SKIPS on a cold model stops spending
180 s heating the runtime this one needs.

**Classification, on evidence: SUITE INTERACTION / RESOURCE CONTENTION.** Not a product regression
(the governed drive, the containment check and the edit all succeeded), not a test-fixture defect in
the ordinary sense (the budget is correct for the condition it was written for), and not
provider-unavailable (no provider turn was refused; a local model was driven to completion).

**W-51 is untouched by it**, structurally: `resolve_model_ref` has exactly two production callers and
neither is on this path.

**OWED, not repaired here:** the live legs share one local-model runtime and nothing serializes them
or declares that they contend. Belongs with the [[U461]]/[[U469]]/[[U472]] assurance-hygiene work,
and the Tier-4 boundary must classify this leg as [[U473]] rather than as an unexplained product
FAIL.

### REPORTING RULE — **every canonical suite report carries its execution mode**

Operator-ruled from [[U472]], and mechanical so the mistake is hard to repeat:

    pytest execution mode: full | -x | focused
    collected: · passed: · failed: · skipped: · exit code:

**An `-x` result is DIAGNOSTIC EVIDENCE ONLY and can never be quoted as the tree-wide failure
count.** A canonical suite record comes from the completed suite, never from an `-x` run — which is
exactly how "one failing test" was reported when the tree had four.

### U474 — **W-52 (R-48): a version counts only when it is a declaration**

**CLOSED at `1f95086`.** Both probes took `splitlines()[0]` and handed that ONE line to a parser
that `search`ed it for the first semver anywhere. It failed in BOTH directions at once, measured
through `probe_provider_cli`:

    '> agy@1.1.9 start' + 'grok 0.2.118'                  -> (1,1,9)  from the BANNER
    'npm WARN update available 1.2.3 -> 2.0.0' + 'grok..'  -> (1,2,3)  the npm OLD version
    'npm WARN update available 9.9.9 -> 10.0.0' alone      -> (9,9,9)  meets_minimum=TRUE

**The first case is sharper than "a missed version": it returned the BANNER's version as the
provider's.** And searching every line instead fixes only that one and makes the other two worse —
verified, the naive whole-text search returns the same wrong answers for both npm cases.

**Declaration shapes admitted, read off the existing fixtures and no others:** BARE `1.1.9` (agy),
NAMED `grok 0.2.118 (1e1687c1cf)` / `codex-cli 0.144.6` / `opencode 0.99.0-mock`. Deriving the
anchor from the two adversarial npm transcripts would have been training the parser on its own exam
questions. Two structural rules: a declaration SHAPE, and EXACTLY ONE version — `old -> new` is a
comparison.

**DECLARED BOUND, and it does not reopen the unit:** a line naming some OTHER program in the same
shape (a hypothetical `npm 10.0.0` alone) would be accepted. Anchoring on provider identity would
close it and is deliberately not done — `agy` prints a BARE version with no identity to anchor on,
and `codex-cli` is not spelled `codex`. Antigravity's bare output is what blocks a universal
provider-name requirement, and inventing provider-specific identity policy to reach philosophical
purity is not warranted.

**Duplication checked before editing**, per [[U468]]: `parse_version` was already single, but the
`splitlines()[0]` policy was written out TWICE, once per probe. `extract_version` now returns the
declaration LINE and its tuple from one pass, both probes call it, and the version SHOWN to the
operator is the line that was PARSED — where before the displayed string and the tuple could come
from different lines.

### U475 — **W-53 (R-38): MEASURED / NO ADDITIONAL PRODUCTION REPAIR REQUIRED**

**CLOSED at `6d21cfe`. No production byte changed.** R-38 was already closed CAUSALLY by W-03/A-2;
what was missing was EVIDENCE. Nothing asserted the PARITY, so a future edit to either runner could
have reopened the divergence silently.

Both live execution paths already pin `encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"` —
`process_tree.run_managed_process` (both platform branches) and
`frontier_provider_recon.subprocess_runner`.

**BEHAVIOURAL, not a source assertion.** Each test spawns a REAL child writing REAL bytes: ASCII,
valid non-ASCII UTF-8 (Latin accents AND CJK), and a lone `0xFF` that is invalid UTF-8 anywhere and
undefined in cp1252. Both paths return a `str` (never `None`, never an exception), preserve the
Unicode as CHARACTERS, replace the malformed sequence, and — the assertion the item asks for —
RETURN THE SAME TEXT. Agreement alone would be satisfied by two identically wrong readers, so the
shared answer is additionally pinned to `PAYLOAD.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")`, and a cp1252
mojibake assertion is explicit because a host-codepage decode still returns a `str`.

**The other half inherited from 0.3 is pinned too:** exit 0 with no READABLE stream must not
classify SUCCESS, together with the distinction the classifier keeps — `None` is the ABSENCE of a
stream and fails closed, `""` is a command that genuinely said nothing and still succeeds.

**CALIBRATED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS**, because a no-repair disposition with an uncalibrated test is a
celebration rather than a measurement:

| calibration | result |
|---|---|
| recon runner `errors="replace"` → `"strict"` | **RED** — `assert 'ready' in ''` |
| process_tree `encoding="utf-8"` → `"cp1252"` | **RED** — `café 会议记录` came back as `cafÃ© ä¼š…` |

Both restored BYTE-IDENTICALLY. The second reproduces the exact historical mechanism A-2 fixed, so
the instrument demonstrably detects the thing it exists to detect. **Mutation H25 makes the recon
side permanent** rather than a one-off calibration.

**NOT CLAIMED:** that the MCP stdio path shares this policy. It deliberately does not — W-04 pins
that one to `strict`, because there the bytes become persisted content with hashes over them.

**RECORDED GAP, not repaired:** `adapters/frontier/process_tree.py` is anchored by no mutation
harness, so only the recon side of the parity is permanently graded. Belongs with the
[[U461]]/[[U469]] assurance-hygiene work.

### U476 — **W-54 (R-85): the argv guard inspects FLAGS, not values**

**CLOSED at `a4feaeb`.** `_flag_pairs` made a NAME candidate out of EVERY token, so a legitimate
model slug spelling one of our flag names was refused. Measured, each as `--model <slug>`:
`tools`, `agent`, `allow`, `worktree`, `dangerously-skip-permissions` → `ValueError`.

**A provider is free to name a model `tools`; this build is not free to refuse it for resembling one
of OUR flag names.** The repair is one condition: a NAME candidate must be DASH-PREFIXED.

**Checked before choosing the rule**, because "dashes only" could have opened a subcommand hole:
every entry in `FORBIDDEN_PROVIDER_ARGS` is a FLAG, read off this host's captured `--help`. None is
a bare subcommand, so skipping non-dash tokens cannot let a forbidden subcommand through.

**It stays safe in the other direction**, which is the property that must not loosen: a token
CARRYING a dash is treated as a flag WHEREVER it appears, so smuggling `--always-approve` in as a
model slug or workdir is still refused. *The value position is what makes a value; a dash is what
makes a flag.* Pinned as its own test — without it the repair would trade one defect for a worse
one. The permission-mode rule still reads a flag's VALUE, which is the one place a value is
authoritative and is keyed to the flag that owns it.

### STANDING DIAGNOSTIC — **if deleting a guard leaves the row GREEN, the test is proving some
### other guard**

Earned twice inside three units and now a default check for every new mutation row:

| unit | what happened |
|---|---|
| [[U471]] W-51 H22 | deleting the empty-inventory branch stayed GREEN — `slug not in inventory` refuses `()` anyway. That branch carries the DIAGNOSTIC, not the refusal. |
| [[U474]] W-52 H24 | deleting the declaration-SHAPE rule stayed GREEN — the exactly-one-version rule refuses the npm notice anyway. |

**A guard whose job is a diagnostic, or whose input is already refused by a neighbouring rule, is
invisible to a row graded by `pytest.raises`.** The fix in both cases was to re-target the row at
the property the guard UNIQUELY carries — and, where the guard's real job was the diagnostic, to
restore the old RETURN VALUE rather than delete the branch.

### U477 — **THE TIER-4 BOUNDARY MATRIX: the three entry points do not disagree**

**BUILT at `2e5d043`. No production byte changed.** Obligation 1 of the boundary, and the answer to
the duplication class this tier kept finding: seven of the eleven units were a surface reading PROSE
for a fact structured evidence already carried, and [[U468]] proved two of those surfaces had
already silently drifted into OPPOSITE auth verdicts for one real `grok models` call. Per-unit tests
pinned each surface against its own expectations. Nothing asserted they AGREE.

One synthetic observation — a `(exit code, stdout, stderr)` triple — is put through the three
PRODUCTION entry points that can reach a control decision about a provider:
`probe_provider_cli`, `probe_status`, and the runtime `FrontierProviderCliBackend.generate`.

**IT IS NOT A FOURTH CLASSIFIER, and that was the hard constraint.** Nothing in the file re-reads a
transcript; no marker list, parser or shape rule is duplicated. Each surface is asked for the
control state it ALREADY PUBLISHES — `ProviderCliProbe.auth_state` / `.selectable_models()`,
`ProviderStatus.state` / `.auth_state` / `.auth_confirmed`, and what `generate` RAISES — and small
projections map those published values onto one vocabulary so they can be compared at all. *A
projection that had to parse anything would be the fourth classifier, and the file would then agree
with itself rather than with the product.* Which pause `generate` raised is read off
`classify_provider_outcome` — the production call `generate` itself makes — never off the message.

**THE INVARIANT IS DELIBERATELY WEAKER THAN EQUALITY.** A probe reports what is KNOWN about a
provider; the runtime reports what happened to ONE invocation. They may REPRESENT a state
differently. They may not DISAGREE:

  * no surface may report a session ASSERTED while another reports authentication BLOCKED;
  * if any surface reports BLOCKED, no surface may PERMIT execution;
  * if no surface reports BLOCKED, no surface may pause ON AUTHENTICATION — [[U467]]/W-48's defect,
    which takes a whole node down.

Equality IS asserted for the one pair where it is the contract: the two probes are two CALLERS of
one policy, so across every row their `auth_state`, `models` and `default_model` must be the SAME
value.

| observation | probe CLI | probe status | runtime |
|---|---|---|---|
| genuine authenticated declaration | AUTHENTICATED, offers `grok-4.5` | AVAILABLE, `auth_confirmed` | returns |
| conditional login prose only | UNVERIFIED | UNVERIFIED, `auth_confirmed` false | returns; nothing inferred |
| explicit signed-out (nonzero) | AUTH_REQUIRED, offers nothing | AUTH_REQUIRED | **ProviderAuthPause** |
| ordinary success discussing auth | UNVERIFIED, inventory empty | same | returns, no pause |
| ordinary success discussing rate limits | UNVERIFIED, inventory empty | same | returns, no pause |
| genuine rate-limit failure | PROBE_FAILED (not an auth verdict) | PROBE_FAILED | **pause, USAGE_LIMIT** |
| malformed/error listing prose | no model invented | same inventory | `resolve_model_ref` REFUSES every token |

**THE ANTI-SHADOW ROW IS THE DECISIVE ONE.** The structured verdict says AUTH_REQUIRED while the
600-char excerpt `generate` used to re-scan provably carries NO auth or usage marker — and it pauses
anyway. **The excerpt's innocence is asserted FIRST**, so the row cannot pass by the runtime
coincidentally re-deriving the pause from prose. That is W-50/H20 preserved at the tier boundary,
and it is the row that distinguishes CONSUMPTION of a verdict from lucky re-derivation.

**ONE ASYMMETRY IS CHARACTERIZED RATHER THAN REPAIRED, and the reasoning is attached to the
measurement so a later reader does not "fix" it into a contradiction.** Grok 0.2.118 exits **ZERO**
when signed out and still lists the public default model. The probes read that through the CLI's
declared auth surface and report AUTH_REQUIRED; the runtime classifier is exit-code-FIRST by
directive section 6 and does not demote a zero exit — the property W-48 exists to protect. **They
answer different questions**: the probes answer *may this provider be OFFERED*, the runtime answers
*did this invocation succeed*. They are compatible **because the auth verdict fences the LAUNCH** —
with AUTH_REQUIRED `selectable_models()` is empty, so no node exists to make the call whose zero
exit would be honoured. That containment is ASSERTED through `_op12_inventory`, not assumed: if the
picker ever stopped consulting `selectable_models()`, the test fails and the asymmetry becomes a
real disagreement.

**IT PASSED 23/23 ON ITS FIRST RUN, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHEN AN INSTRUMENT MUST BE CALIBRATED RATHER
THAN BELIEVED.** Three rows added to `_op18e_hardening_mutations.py`, PERMANENT rather than run once
and discarded, each restoring a defect this tier actually shipped and each graded by the ONE matrix
row that uniquely carries the property:

| row | restored defect | grader |
|---|---|---|
| H27 | `classify_models_call` parses the auth evidence and DROPS it (W-49/R-08) | the containment row |
| H28 | `generate` re-derives the pause from the excerpt (W-50/R-24) | the anti-shadow row |
| H29 | the picker offers the raw inventory, not the selectable one | the containment row |

**All three RED. `_op18e_hardening` is now 29/29 RED, all restores byte-identical.**

**NOT CLAIMED, and the distinction matters.** H27 and H28 overlap in territory with the existing
H18 and H19. Those calibrate the PER-UNIT tests; these calibrate the MATRIX. Neither new row found
a new defect and neither is offered as one — what they establish is that the boundary instrument
detects the things it exists to detect, which an uncalibrated green never establishes.

### U478 — **CORRECTION to [[U472]]: the three Ollama legs are NOT a cold-model readiness condition**

[[U472]] classified three live Ollama generation legs as a genuine COLD-MODEL READINESS defect, on
the strength of one distinguishing measurement: that they fail *even in isolation* while [[U473]]'s
OpenCode leg passes there. **On a genuinely quiet host that measurement does not reproduce.**

    tests/integration/test_assembled_roster.py::test_item7_ollama_smoke_runs_live      PASS   31.80s
    tests/integration/test_multi_model_adapters.py::test_live_ollama_backend_smoke     PASS    8.17s
    tests/integration/test_assembled_run.py::..._live_ollama_leg_or_skip_with_record   PASS    3.83s

**AND ITS STATED PREMISE IS FALSE ON ITS OWN TERMS.** [[U472]] reasons that *"the listed models are
17–67 GB, so a non-resident model cannot load inside that budget"*. These legs never touch those
models. `_SMOKE_MODELS = ("qwen2.5:7b-instruct", "qwen2.5:14b-instruct") + _REASONING_MODELS` and
`pick_model` takes an EXACT tag match in preference order, so on this host it selects
**`qwen2.5:14b-instruct`, 9.0 GB** — never `llama4:scout` (67 GB) or `mistral-medium-3.5` (80 GB).
`ollama ps` confirms `qwen2.5:14b-instruct` as the model actually loaded. It cold-loaded AND
generated in 31.8 s against a 180 s budget.

**What [[U472]] measured was host load, and it attributed it to model SIZE.** Its own text already
carries the confounder — *"on a machine under sustained load"* — and it was written in a session
where the same suite went from 642 s to 4805 s. **A "focused" run made inside that window was not an
isolated run**, so the isolation axis the classification turns on was never actually varied. *That
this is the mechanism is a hypothesis consistent with the evidence; that the classification does not
hold is a measurement.*

**CONSEQUENCE FOR WHAT IS OWED.** [[U472]] proposed a 60 s session-cached generation-readiness probe
so these legs SKIP-WITH-RECORD instead of failing. **That instrument would be aimed at the wrong
condition** — there is no readiness condition to detect; the prerequisite is satisfied and the model
generates well inside budget. What remains is the contention item [[U473]] already named, and
[[U473]] also already ruled out the wrong answer to it: a skip criterion meaning *"the host is
busy"* is the one general "external stuff seems unhappy" switch that must not be built. **The honest
owed item is serialization of the live legs, or nothing at all** — see [[U480]].

**NOT a product finding, and nothing reopens.** No code was implicated then and none is now; W-51
remains untouched by it on the structural ground [[U472]] itself established.

### U481 — **W-55 (R-09): the capability check may fail, but the server may not vanish**

**CLOSED at `cee1e84`.** The MCP stdio server resolved the app-control capability BEFORE reading a
single frame of stdin, and exited 2 on any failure, to a stderr the launching CLI discards.
Measured pre-repair on this host [OBSERVED]: against an unreachable gateway the process exits 2
with EMPTY stdout — `initialize` never answered — and the only diagnosis is `sovereign MCP startup
refused: ToolError: Sovereign app-control channel failed: <urlopen error [WinError 10061] …>`.
That is R-09's confirmed shape (exit 2 in 0.45 s no-env, 2.5 s closed port), and it renders on the
conductor side as *"MCP server 'sovereign' was not ready for this step."*

The repair: the FIRST FRAME is answered before any capability round-trip; the round-trip then runs
eagerly AFTER that first answered frame, and its failure DEGRADES rather than kills: the fault is
appended to a bounded JSON-lines file `<store root>/mcp_startup_faults.log` (1 MiB cap — the
W-35/W-63 class — stderr still gets a copy), every tool call answers with a structured `isError`
payload naming the fault and the durable record, and the resolution is retried per call, so a
gateway that comes up later is recovered by the next call, not by a restart. No exit-2 path
remains.

**WHY THE EAGER ROUND-TRIP SURVIVES AT ALL:** the worker admission chain reads this process's
first gateway arrival as evidence of life — `worker-readiness.js`'s MCP_CONNECTING loop STALLS a
worker whose session never establishes (`mcp_readiness_timeout` → STALLED within the 120 s
`MCP_READINESS_TIMEOUT_MS`), and `assignment-gate.js` refuses assignment with `mcp_never_connected`.
Deferring the check fully would have stalled every spawned worker at readiness; the defect was the
FATAL failure mode, not the round-trip. The desktop handshake test still observes
`connectionState "connected"` deterministically: warm runs before `tools/list` is answered.

**Evidence.** Negative tests proven FAILING against pre-repair code [OBSERVED]:
`test_initialize_is_answered_when_the_capability_is_unreachable` → *"AssertionError: the server
answered nothing and exited 2: a capability failure must not silence the handshake"*;
`test_a_capability_failure_is_structured_for_the_client_and_logged_durably` → `assert 2 in {}`
(no reply to the tool call at all). Both fail BEHAVIOURALLY, not symbolically. The healthy-gateway
controls (round-trip works; session established with no tool call) passed PRE-repair as well —
CONTROL / INHERITED, preserved rather than repaired. Focused: 136 passed across the seven
MCP/collaboration/write-path suites; `apps/desktop` `sovereign-mcp-stdio.test.js` 1 pass.
Mutation: `_op19_5_write_path_mutations.py` gains row W55 — 24/24 RED, all restores byte-identical,

### U485 — **W-59: `record_synthesis` can no longer complete a task over an OPEN debate — [[U410]] CLOSED**

**CLOSED at `c92a51e`.** [[U410]], carried since 19.5: `record_synthesis` enforced only the
completeness rule and would move a task to COMPLETED while a debate on it was still OPEN — the
round-1 validator's probe P2 did exactly that through the service and got `'COMPLETED'` back. The
U332 gate guarded the TOOL path only, so invariant 16 ("failed artifacts cannot advance") was
enforced at the boundary, not at the state transition — the [[U326]] shape: the rule in one place
and the write in another. "Not exploitable in the product today" was the mitigation then; the rule
now lives where the write is.

**The repair.** Inside `record_synthesis`'s write fence — on the rows the transaction actually
reads — the gate refuses while any debate on the task is OPEN. Checked anywhere else it would be a
race (the doctrine `_assert_legal_transition` records); the debate read is on the fence's own
connection (`list_operational_debates` takes no write lock), so it sees the debates as of the
transaction's serialization point. Semantics mirror the tool path EXACTLY: OPEN blocks; CLOSED
passes; ABORTED does NOT — a deliberation that can no longer conclude must not hold the task
forever ([[U416]]), and the tool path reports it separately.

**ORDERING, said exactly:** the gate runs AFTER the completeness check. Both are state gates inside
the same fence, so the order decides only WHICH reason a doubly-refused call hears, never whether
it is refused. Completeness stays first because its verdict is deterministic and pinned in the
delegation matrix; debate ids are random (`secrets.token_hex`), so a matrix cell quoting the gate's
message could never be pinned. The first draft placed the gate first and the pinned matrix FAILED —
correctly; the reorder is the repair that keeps the matrix honest without regenerating it. The tool
path checks debates first at the boundary; the service's ordering is its own, and NEITHER layer can
complete a task over an OPEN debate.

**Evidence.** Negative test proven FAILING against pre-repair code [OBSERVED]:
`test_record_synthesis_is_refused_while_a_debate_on_the_task_is_open` → *"Failed: DID NOT RAISE
\<class CollaborationError\>"* — the service returned COMPLETED over the open debate (U410's P2
shape, aimed at the service). Declared bounds passed PRE-repair as well (a CLOSED debate does not
block; an ABORTED debate does not) — CONTROL / INHERITED, now pinned. Focused: 114 passed across
the collaboration / delegation / write-path suites, the pinned matrix UNCHANGED. Mutation:
`_op19_5_write_path_mutations.py` row W59 (the whole gate block deleted) — 26/26 RED, all restores
byte-identical; `_op19_policy_delegation_mutations.py` 40/40 RED, all restores byte-identical.

**Prose repaired with the code:** two sites in `collaboration_service.py` described the absent
gate as current state (the module-level debate-state note; `abort_debate`'s SCOPE paragraph). Both
now state the guard exists at the transition, history preserved. **NOT CLAIMED:** the tool path's
broader rules (every CLOSED debate must be named, no foreign debates) stay tool-layer concerns —
they govern the shape of the conductor's CLAIM, not the legality of the transition. The residual
U410 asymmetry (`record_candidate` accepts an ABORTED debate in `debates_considered` while the
conductor may not count it) is untouched by this unit and stays recorded in [[U410]]'s own text.

retraction, and it is written where the universal sentence lived:

**The repair.** `schemas/README.md` — the opening claim is rescoped to what the files GROUND, and

every write, fenced transition legality, tool-layer `inputSchema`); how it changes
(successor-schema ruling only). Pinned beside the negative test: the mismatch fact above, and the

### U489 — **W-62: [[U434]] CLOSED — a node can now be VERIFIED, not only provoked**

**CLOSED at `5383423`.** [[U434]], opened by 19.7: no server->node ping and no node heartbeat, so
an idle-but-healthy worker could not be verified when a conductor wanted to assign to it — only
provoked (`send_message`, whose delivery the U328 gate may withhold) or waited for; and
`_lastSeen` observes gateway-mediated calls only, so a node doing store-only MCP work went stale
WHILE WORKING. U434 named its own closure: "A heartbeat the node makes on a cadence shorter than
the staleness window closes both." This row records it taken.

**The repair.** `NodeHeartbeat` in `mcp_server/sovereign_tools.py`, started by
`_DeferredRuntime._build` the moment a node's capability resolves — an ESTABLISHED node, the only
kind U434's silence misled anyone about — beating on the gateway's `identity` operation. That
operation is chosen, not improvised: the gateway stamps `_lastSeen` for ANY authenticated request
before dispatch, and `identity` answers without a handler and WITHOUT an `_recordOperation` entry
— a liveness beat is not work, so it must not appear in the node's operation history. No new
gateway operation exists for this on purpose: the protocol addition is the node's cadence, not a
second surface to govern. The gateway half is already pinned by the desktop suite
(`sovereign-control-server.test.js`: an `identity` call over real HTTP reads `connected`).

**KEY EQUIVALENCE the evidence relies on:** from the gateway's point of view, store-only work and
idleness are the SAME silence — neither produces a gateway arrival. Proving the heartbeat keeps an
idle node fresh proves it keeps a store-only-working node fresh; the control test pins the other
half (a store write reaches the store and NOT the gateway; without a beat the evidence ages out).

**Bounded three ways:** the beat's HTTP call carries its own short timeout (`AppControlClient.call`
grows an optional timeout; never the client's 180 s ceiling — a liveness probe that could block
for the ceiling defeats itself); `stop()` has a budget it reports rather than exceeds; the thread
is a daemon, so a heartbeat can never hold the process open. A failed beat is swallowed and
returns False — a heartbeat that could break a tool call or crash the node would be worse than the
silence it removes. **Cadence:** 60 s default, inside the gateway's 180 s window with a missed
beat still inside it; `SOVEREIGN_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_S` overrides it. **NOT AUTHORIZATION:** a beat
proves reachability with the node's own credential, nothing about what it may do (invariant 7).

**Evidence.** Negative test proven FAILING against pre-repair code [OBSERVED]:
`test_an_established_node_keeps_itself_verifiably_alive_without_being_provoked` → *"AssertionError:
U434: an established node has no way to keep itself verifiably alive — it can only be provoked or
waited for"*. Control passed PRE-repair as well (INHERITED mechanics, pinned beside the repair).
Declared bounds: a beat against a dead gateway is swallowed (False, no raise); stop inside its
budget; the deferred runtime starts the cadence on resolution. Adjacent suites 134 passed.
Mutation: `_op19_5` row W62 (the beat keeps its bookkeeping but never reaches the gateway) —
29/29 RED, all restores byte-identical; `_op19_policy_delegation` 40/40 RED, all restores
byte-identical.

**NOT CLAIMED:** that a never-established node is verified — it reads `configured`/`disconnected`
exactly as before. U434's refusal wording (UNVERIFIED, never failure; clears on the next gateway
call) is unchanged — and now a beat IS a gateway call.

### U491 — **CARRIED DEBT: Codex 0.146.0 cannot express the MCP server `cwd` without an installation-specific absolute path**

Routed here by operator ruling 2026-08-20 — **explicitly NOT to W-77**. [[U483]] / W-57 keeps its
**CLOSED** disposition; this is the portability residue, **CARRIED, not open**.

**Measured offline on this host** [OBSERVED], `codex-cli 0.146.0`, no provider call and no live
spawn — the CLI's own surfaces only:

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| `codex mcp add --help` | **no `cwd` option exists at all** — zero case-insensitive matches. The key is config-file-only |
| `codex mcp get sovereign` | echoes `cwd: D:/multi model terminal app/sovereign-orchestration-workspace` **verbatim** — no normalization, no resolution |
| `-c mcp_servers.sovereign.cwd="."` | accepted, stored **literally** as `.` |
| `-c ...cwd="./"` | accepted, stored literally as `./` |
| `-c ...cwd="~/x"` | **`~X:/`** — tilde is NOT expanded, and the value is mangled |
| `-c ...cwd="${PWD}"` | literal — **no environment interpolation** |
| `-c ...cwd="%CD%"` | literal — no Windows interpolation |

**So the absolute pin is the only expressible form in this CLI version.** A relative value parses but
is stored literally and would resolve against **Codex's own** startup directory — reproducing
**N-02** precisely, which is the condition W-57 exists to remove.

**Bounding tripwire, recorded as such and NOT as a fix:**
`tests/unit/test_mcp_registration_provenance.py:59-65` extracts the `cwd` by regex and asserts it
equals THIS repository's root computed at test time. The GRADER is portable even though the VALUE is
not, so a moved repository fails **LOUDLY** rather than silently — which is the property W-57
claimed and which holds.

**Why not W-77.** W-77 is scoped to the runtime EMISSION of absolute host paths in refusal reasons
and the authorization record. This is a **static, tracked configuration value**, not an emission, and
folding it into an emission unit would put an unfixable item inside a unit that can close.

**Disposition: CARRIED. Revisited if and when Codex gains the capability** — a `--cwd` flag, config
interpolation, or config-file-relative resolution. Until then no repair exists to make, and
manufacturing one would be inventing portability the tool does not have.

### U492 — **OPEN: the PYTHON mutation-harness family self-pins on-disk bytes and therefore CANNOT fail closed**

Found 2026-08-20 while verifying the [[U481]] harness incident (Tier-5 acceptance item A11).
Registered SEPARATELY from [[U461]] by operator ruling, because it is the **opposite** failure mode.

**The defect** [OBSERVED]. `tools/mutation/_op19_policy_delegation_mutations.py:341`:

    _PINNED.setdefault(ROOT / rel, (ROOT / rel).read_bytes())

The harness pins **whatever bytes are on disk at startup**. It carries no external expected
SHA-256. Restores are then compared against that self-pin (`:299`, `:308`, `:318`), so a run
guarantees only that each file returns to *whatever it started as* — contaminated or not.

**It is the whole family, not one harness** [OBSERVED, all twelve checked this date]: `_op12`,
`_op13`, `_op18c_close`, `_op18c_probe_path`, `_op18d_amendment`, `_op18d_close`,
`_op18e_electron_wiring`, `_op18e_hardening`, `_op18e_live_acceptance`, `_op18e_live_shape`,
`_op19_5_write_path`, `_op19_policy_delegation` — every one reads its baseline from disk, and
**none carries a hardcoded expected hash**.

**The observed instance is already in the record.** [[U481]]: a run killed mid-row left
`sovereign_tools.py` MUTATED, and *"the re-run pinned the contaminated bytes as its baseline and
reported P22 GREEN"* — a plausible **39/40** rather than an error.

**THE ASYMMETRY, stated explicitly.** [[U453]] records that the **JS** harnesses pin the baseline
they may run against and **REFUSE** rather than adopt a mutation as their baseline:

| family | behaviour on an already-mutated tree |
|---|---|
| **JS** — `pane_input_bypass`, `system_pane_write`, `readiness_signal`, `orchestration`, `disarm_authority` | **REFUSES** ([[U453]]) |
| **Python** — all twelve above | **ADOPTS the tree as truth** |

[[U461]] is a harness that could not START and reported nothing. This is a harness that
**CERTIFIES A TREE IT NEVER VERIFIED**. Per [[U469]]'s standing rule a plausible partial is worse
than a refusal; this is worse again, because the number is not even partial — it is complete, and
wrong.

**SCOPE, stated honestly and DELIBERATELY NOT QUANTIFIED.** Every Python mutation-harness result in
this programme is **conditional on the tree having been clean at harness start, and that
precondition was never verified.** How many results are affected cannot be determined from the
record, and an estimate would be worse than this statement.

**COMPENSATING CONTROL — IN FORCE IMMEDIATELY**, operator ruling 2026-08-20, no further
authorization required:

> **Verify the worktree CLEAN BEFORE every mutation-harness run, not only after, and state the
> pre-run verification in the harness report. A harness run without a stated pre-run verification
> is not evidence.**

The companion directive's §11.2 already requires the after; the BEFORE is what this defect needs.

**SEQUENCING — BINDING.** Pulled forward as a **Tier 6 PRECONDITION** (§A gains a fifth), removed
from W-78's scope and from the [[U461]] slot. Seventeen Tier 6 units each generate harness evidence
through this instrument; running them first manufactures seventeen units of conditional evidence.

**The repair is NOT designed here.** When it is authorized the property is [[U461]]'s, extended: the
validation surface must distinguish **HARNESS RAN AND CAUGHT ALL** from **HARNESS COULD NOT START**,
and now also from **HARNESS CERTIFIED A TREE IT DID NOT VERIFY** — and it must not become another
supervisory layer for the supervisors.

### U494 — **OWED AT ACCEPTANCE: `conductor/DEBATE_POLICY.md` attributes debate bounds to a service the MCP path does not reach**

Recorded 2026-08-20 by operator ruling, during the Tier-5 acceptance backlog. **The file is NOT
edited** — see the disposition below.

**The claim.** `conductor/DEBATE_POLICY.md:8` reads *"Bounds (**service-enforced**, I-DS1): ≤5
rounds, early stop on convergence, per-debate budget, per-caller quota, global concurrent cap."*

**Measured, both sides** [OBSERVED]:

| Bound | `debate_service` | MCP collaboration path |
|---|---|---|
| ≤5 rounds | ENFORCED — `round_manager/manager.py:5` | ENFORCED — range-check `collaboration_service.py:286-287`, applied `:337` |
| early stop on convergence | ENFORCED — `manager.py:69-71` | absent |
| per-debate budget | ENFORCED — `service.py:74-77` (CostGovernor) | **recorded, never read** — `collaboration_service.py:291` |
| per-caller quota | ENFORCED — `service.py:74-77` | absent |
| global concurrent cap | ENFORCED — `service.py:74-77` | absent |

**`debate_service` enforces five of five. The MCP collaboration path enforces one of five**, and
`collaboration_service.py:297` says so in its own words: *"`max_rounds` is the only bound."*

**THE DEFECT IS ATTRIBUTION, NOT FABRICATION.** Every bound the document names is genuinely
implemented somewhere. What the document does not say is **where** — and the unqualified phrase
*"service-enforced"* reads, to a conductor operating over the 16-tool MCP surface, as a description
of the path it is actually on. `debate_service` is unreachable from that surface ([[U349]],
[[U488]]).

**Convergence-stop is implemented, and is STRICTER than its own phrase** — recorded because it is
the one place in this programme where the code is more careful than the document describing it.
`_converged()` (`manager.py:86-90`) requires **at least two voices** — *"a single voice is not
concurrence"* — and requires the alignment to rest on **at least one supported position**. The
document says "early stop on convergence"; the code will not stop early on a lone unsupported
assertion.

**DISPOSITION: OWED AT ACCEPTANCE. The file is deliberately left unedited**, by operator ruling, on
two grounds recorded together with the counterargument:

  1. The file's own first line disclaims binding: *"**DRAFT v0.1** (2026-07-16) — operator-authored
     asset… This draft was prepared for operator review during Phase 0; **it binds nothing until the
     operator accepts it.**"*
  2. `conductor/` files are `conductor_files` in the Phase-0 freeze and `conductor_file_write_
     authority` is **operator-only**. An edit costs a manifest regeneration, a `freeze_integrity_
     sha256` move, an `operator_signature` reset to PENDING, and the operator-only transcription
     procedure — for a document that governs nothing today.

**The counterargument is recorded and is not weak:** *"it binds nothing"* is adjacent to the
reasoning that let other false claims survive in this tree. The distinction the ruling rests on is
the **explicit disclaimer in the document's own first line**, which `CLAUDE.md:51` — the live
instruction file, carrying the same invariant-17 over-claim — does **not** have.

**So the correction is a PRECONDITION OF ACCEPTING THE DRAFT**, not a repair owed now. Whoever
accepts DEBATE_POLICY.md out of DRAFT status applies the correction in the same act, or accepts a
document that misattributes enforcement.

**PRE-AGREED WORDING** (operator-ratified as preferred, to be applied only if and when the edit is
authorized). Verified accurate across all five bounds as of this reading:

    Bounds (I-DS1): ≤5 rounds, early stop on convergence, per-debate budget, per-caller quota,
    global concurrent cap — enforced by `debate_service`. On the MCP collaboration debate path
    only the round bound is enforced; `budget_units` is recorded and never read (U349, OPEN).

**RELATED, NOT DUPLICATED.** [[U349]] is the unenforced invariant; [[U488]] is W-61's recording of
it at the code; [[U493]] is W-61's disposition correction. This row is the **documentary** surface
only, and it is the lesser of the two: `CLAUDE.md:51` carries the same over-claim with no
disclaimer and is separately authorized for correction.

### U495 - **OPEN: `open_debate` accepts a COMPLETED task, and a debate can then be opened AND turned on terminal work**

Found 2026-08-22 by C-5 case (b), the W-59 addendum's second probe. Registered per PARK-NEW:
**deliberately NOT repaired inside C-5** - it is outside the 84 and outside the loop directive's
named repairs. Case (a)'s forced-ordering instrument landed first (`369beee`) and asserts the
residual only as an observed ordering fact.

**The finding** [OBSERVED, this date]. `CollaborationService.open_debate`
(`mcp_server/collaboration_service.py:273-313`) checks caller authority, task EXISTENCE
(`_require_task`), participants, `max_rounds`, `budget_units` and the proposition - and never the
task's STATE. Driven against a legitimately completed task:

    task status after legitimate synthesis: COMPLETED
    CASE-B RESULT: ACCEPTED - open_debate created d-eb86879cc9542005 state: OPEN on a COMPLETED task
    CASE-B DEEPER: post_debate_turn accepted: turn-d91e9ab65b57af9c

So terminal work can acquire a NEW OPEN debate and accumulate turns afterwards. Consequences that
follow without any further defect: the W-59/U410 gate then blocks every future legitimate
`record_synthesis` on this task until someone closes or aborts the late debate (an OPEN debate is
a permanent hold on re-synthesis); inspector feeds report an open debate on finished work; and the
turn deadline machinery arms over a task nobody is executing.

**Why W-59 does not cover it.** W-59's property is directional: no synthesis may complete OVER an
open debate. It says nothing about debates arriving AFTER completion. C-5 case (a) proved the two
cannot interleave inside the fence (exclusion carried by TWO layers [OBSERVED]: the store's
Python `_write_lock` and SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` - nulling the Python lock left the opener
blocked >10 s inside SQLite with the fence still seeing zero debates), which means the ONLY way a
debate overlaps completed work is this post-completion entrance.

**Scope notes.** The tool path reaches this through the same service method, so the conductor's
MCP surface can do this too. `_considered_debates` refusal vocabulary is unaffected. Related,
NOT duplicated: [[U410]] closed by W-59 at [[U485]]; [[U349]] (budget unenforced); [[U493]]
(W-61 disposition). This row is the TERMINAL-STATE entrance, a distinct property from all three.

**Owner: operator ruling required.** Options visible from the tree, none taken: refuse
`open_debate` on tasks in terminal states (mirrors the transition table's fail-closed shape);
allow-but-mark (debate on COMPLETED records its provenance and does not block re-synthesis); or
rule it intended (a post-completion review channel) and pin THAT behaviour deliberately. A
defensive try/except for the blocking consequence alone would treat the symptom and is not
recommended here.
---
